Generated by `game/tools/chronicle.gd` on the full simulation (economy, companies, law, staff, politics). The player's party (Founders') runs on autoplay. Month m0 = January, Year 1; parties form in Year 3; elections every 4 years plus any extra elections.

Contents: 1 Summary · 2 Parties (why each appeared) · 3 Governments · 4 Elections (campaign and every voter group) · 5 Bills and decisions · 6 Lever changes · 7 Year-by-year condition · 8 Event log · 9 Unions, trade, industry and the press

## What changed since the last chronicles (v4), and what is still to come

These chronicles (v5, seeds 1–3) ran on the build of 2026-11-13 (commit a2acc09). New since v4: section 9
(unions, trade, industry, the press) and a trade-balance column in the year table.

### Changed since v4

**Unions are real organisations (your decision A41)**
- **The unions:**
  - named sector unions (Miners, Builders, Plant Workers, Farm Workers, Public Servants, Shop & Service, Professionals);
  - a Colony Federation of Labour;
  - members from the real workforce, and dues funds;
  - leaders elected every 4 years, from militant to moderate;
  - rare mergers and rank-and-file breakaways.
- **Disputes:**
  - grievances build until a union makes a demand;
  - the employer answers: a company by its profits and boss, an AI government by ideology, and you when you govern;
  - failed talks can lead to a strike, paid from the strike fund;
  - a strike ends won, compromised or lost, and an empty fund collapses it;
  - there is arbitration, and a rare general strike.
  - A deal calms a union for about two years.
- **Politics:**
  - each union backs a pro-labour party by its own issues;
  - unions donate in election years;
  - a party that cuts union rights, wages or benefits is dropped (about once per union every 18 years);
  - union members volunteer in campaigns.
- **Laws:** strike ballots, closed shop, public-sector strikes, compulsory recognition, damages for unlawful strikes, the political levy, and essential services (minimum service or no strike).

**New demand: exports, consumer industries, quality (your decision A42)**
- **Exports on every ship** at home-world prices, minus freight, the export tax and the home world's levy:
  - companies stockpile at the port between ships, and depots limit the space;
  - merchants bring back only goods that will sell;
  - the home world can reserve goods or claim a levy, and the colony can refuse its terms.
- **Consumer industries:**
  - clothing, furnishings and fine food, from textile mills, furniture works and bakeries;
  - household stocks wear out, and cheap goods faster;
  - there's no spending cap, so idle savings get spent;
  - buying follows confidence, booming and slumping;
  - each workshop has a quality, reputation follows it, the top tier pays the luxury tax, and shoddy goods cause scandals;
  - exports are priced by quality.
- **Tourist sites** exist on the planet (Terra), but tourists don't come yet (transport, below).

**Unemployment and the economy (Bob)**
- **No overbuilding:** firms stop investing in a good once capacity is well above demand.
- **Public works** grow with how strongly a government believes in them: housing, schools, clinics and roads.
- **A public jobs scheme**, set by parliament, as a last resort at 80% of a basic wage.
- **New builders** are founded when public contracts sit unbid.
- **Maintenance first:** cash-poor farms keep their plants running.
- **No forced-sale loops:** a plant that can't be restored is scrapped.
- **Administrators** keep companies running.
- **Failed plants** go only to same-industry buyers, a workers' co-op, or closure.
- **Famine fixes:**
  - struck farms keep 60% running;
  - bakeries buy food only at prices their cakes can pay;
  - shortage and famine news names the big company buyers.
- **Retirement age is a law** (55–72, default 62), and parliament can now table it.
- **Bob's 6-colony test before this run:**
  - healthy-economy months 6,238 (previous best 5,948);
  - mean unemployment 16.8% (was about 20%);
  - population 3,250–3,580 at Year 100;
  - no defaults.

**Politics fixes from the v4 review**
- **Confidence-and-supply prices** are now on the government's agenda, and only for laws parliament can actually change.
- **Cabinet discipline:** coalition parties vote yes on their government's bills, or abstain on matters of conscience.
- **No-confidence motions** are not repeated unless something changed.
- **Party splits** happen over each party's own most divisive issue, not always redistribution.
- **Single-issue parties** don't reform while an earlier party still owns the issue.
- **Party names** match why a party formed.
- **A fuller party field is pulled back toward 4–9 parties:** crowded-field mergers, and splinters folding back. This is not a hard limit.
- **Conviction:** a government gives less weight to remedies that go against its beliefs, so parties answer the same crisis differently.
- **Legal handover:** the commander's last ordinances survive the constitution's adoption.
- **Saved games** continue exactly as before saving (integer-only state).

**The press**
- Parties, unions and companies found their own papers, which live and die on their money.
- False reports get exposed, papers investigate, defamation suits are paid as far as possible, and censorship is allowed only in emergencies.

### Not visible in this text, but in the game
- **The Office** (your decision A44): the turn now runs through one desk.
  - Your paper or press digest comes first, then reports, then an inbox of emails from your ~20 named staff.
  - Staff skill and politics shape their advice, and a weak chief of staff can bury things.
  - There are urgent calls, a calendar, office hours, explicit delegation, and hiring by interview with hidden candidate stats.
  - A tabs view works now: tabs you've visited this month are dimmed. The drawn desk view comes next.
- **Windows:** Unions, Trade, the tourist sites on the globe, and the road network on the colony map, with a road-building tool.

### What this run shows (seed 3)
- **One famine month (Year 49).**
- **Unemployment** averages 14.2%.
- **Real income** is the best of the three runs (121–181).
- **Exports**: 50 ships, 79 million credits.
- **Strikes**: 43 over the century, the most militant run. Strikes come in most decades.
- **Governments**: two fall to no-confidence votes.
- **Parties**: 15 founded, 9 at the end.
- **Consumer industry**: the only run with a bakery still standing.

### Known problems in this build
- **Population still grows too slowly**: about 2,450–2,620 adults (roughly 3,300–3,600 people) at Year 100, where
  a young frontier colony should reach 6,000–15,000. There is no baby boom and no retirement wave, because ages
  are not tracked yet. Bob is building an age-structured population model (E120).
- **The consumer industries don't take hold**: by Year 100 seeds 1 and 2 have no textile mill, furniture works or
  bakery at all, and seed 3 has one bakery and one mothballed furniture works. Meanwhile 48–63 service hubs exist
  (plus about 20 mothballed), so new demand ends up there instead. Bob is tracing it.
- **Rival newspapers rarely last**: 15–29 papers are founded per century, but most close (51 of 60 across the three
  runs); 2–4 papers are active at Year 100, and seed 3's Founders' Party Herald survives from Year 19 to the end.
  The union paper is refounded every decade or so. (Corrected after review.) Anni is reworking the papers'
  economics. 228–442 false or misleading reports are exposed per century, which is probably too many.
- **Busy parliaments**: 216–433 bills and 388–845 law changes per century (v4: about 200). Many new laws can now
  be tabled (unions, trade, transport, retirement), but it may be too hyperactive; to watch.
- **Union endorsements churn** more in this table than in Ella's measurement (some re-endorsements may be counted
  twice); being checked.


### Still to come
- **Transport** (your decision A43): Terra has built the road network: tracks, roads, lanes, junctions, bridges, and your rule that nothing is reachable for free. Still to come:
  - freight priced by route;
  - buses and commuting;
  - tour operators with rovers and airships;
  - traffic counts, accidents and the engineers' reports;
  - governments deciding on the reports.
- **Leisure venues** (arenas, parks, theatres, taverns) and **tourists** arriving on the ships.
- **Consumer industries, second pass:** fashion cycles, seasons, and furnishing waves when new housing is built.
- **Colonial goods:** the rare mineral and native crop as the home world's quota.
- **Housing life-cycle and areas driving the economy;** random crises and company greed (hazards); climate damage.
- **The office:** the drawn desk view, visitors and interviews at the door, and the remaining systems moving into emails.
- **A 3D colony view,** after transport.
- **Technology** isn't on the board yet.
